task: Write one word in each gap: So I'm at the bakery, I ___ ___ in the queue, and this woman suddenly ___ round and hands me her dog. (stand / turn)
explanation shown to learner: In a story told in the present, the background is in the present continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*) and the main events in the present simple (*turns, hands*).
explanation in Latvian: Stāstā tagadnē fons ir Present Continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*), bet galvenie notikumi Present Simple (*turns, hands*).

task: In this story, which verb gives the background, not an event that moves the story on? So I'm sitting on the train, this man opens a bag of crisps, everyone turns round, and he just smiles.
explanation shown to learner: In a story told in the present, the background is usually in the present continuous (*I'm sitting on the train*) and the events that move the story on are in the present simple (*opens, turns round, smiles*).
explanation in Latvian: Stāstā tagadnē fons parasti ir Present Continuous (*I'm sitting on the train*), bet notikumi, kas *virza* stāstu, ir Present Simple (*opens, turns round, smiles*).

task: Write one word in each gap: And Jones ___ the ball to Taylor, who ___ and scores! (pass / shoot)
explanation shown to learner: In a live commentary, quick actions that are over as you speak are in the present simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* would describe a longer action in progress.
explanation in Latvian: Tiešraides komentārā ātras darbības, kas beidzas runāšanas brīdī, ir Present Simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* aprakstītu ilgāku darbību, kas vēl notiek.

correct answer: I'm gathering you're looking for a new flat.
wrong options / checks: I hear the bridge will be closed all summer. | Anna tells me you've started running. | It says here the museum is free on Sundays.
explanation shown to learner: To pass on news we have heard or read, we use the present simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here*. Not *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*
explanation in Latvian: Lai nodotu dzirdētu vai izlasītu ziņu, lieto Present Simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here.* Nevis *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*

correct answer: I'm wondering could you check my CV.
wrong options / checks: We're hoping to move in by the end of May. | I'm thinking of joining a gym. | She's always asking me for advice.
explanation shown to learner: After *I'm wondering*, the question becomes *if / whether* + statement order: *I'm wondering whether you could check my CV.*
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *I'm wondering* jautājums kļūst par *if / whether* + apgalvojuma vārdu secību: *I'm wondering whether you could check my CV.*

task: The app ___ to work on my phone. Can you check it? (not / appear)
correct answer: doesn't appear | does not appear | didn't appear | did not appear | appears not
explanation shown to learner: *appear* = seem is a state: present simple, *doesn't appear to work*. In the meaning *take part* it can be continuous (*She's appearing in a musical*).
explanation in Latvian: *appear* = šķist ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *doesn't appear to work*. Nozīmē piedalīties, uzstāties var būt Continuous forma (*She's appearing in a musical*).
answer notes: didn't appear :: Also possible if you mean when you tried it. :: Arī pareizi, ja runā par to, kad mēģināji. || appears not :: Also correct, but more formal. :: Arī pareizi, bet oficiālāk.

task: My sister and her husband ___ their first baby next month. (expect)
explanation shown to learner: *be expecting a baby* = she is pregnant, always continuous. In the meaning *think something will happen*, *expect* is simple (*I expect it will rain*).
explanation in Latvian: *be expecting a baby* = gaida bērnu, vienmēr Continuous forma. Nozīmē domāt, ka kaut kas notiks *expect* ir vienkāršajā formā (*I expect it will rain*).

task: Your friend lent you money and is worried. Choose the most natural way to make a promise: ___ I'll pay you back on Friday.
wrong options / checks: I'm promising | I'm going to promise | I was promising
explanation shown to learner: When saying the words is the act itself, use the present simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.*
explanation in Latvian: Ja paši vārdi ir darbība, lieto Present Simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.*
